extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers preparing or reviewing NIH-style grant applications (R01/resubmission)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and example content for an NIH-style grant resubmission (research strategy, Specific Aims, responses to reviewer criticisms) focused on an R01 in biomedical/physical microbiology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (focus and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original proposal too broad in scope. The resubmission sharpened the focus by making this resubmission only about P. aeruginosa in chronic wounds, rather than polymicrobial infections in multiple anatomical sites of chronic infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address reviewer critique by narrowing scope to a clear, specific organism/site and explicitly state how this concentrated focus increases significance and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (translation between in vivo and in vitro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Difficult to translate results between in vivo and in vitro. Response: Added information on how we will measure disease outcomes (Specific Aim 1) and how we will compare those with our in vitro results (Specific Aim 2). Sketched how to respond if in vivo and in vitro results do not correspond (page 10). New Activity 3-3 gives an in vivo validation of the most novel in vitro results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain explicitly how in vitro studies will be compared and validated against in vivo outcomes and include contingency/validation plans if results diverge (e.g., in vivo validations of key in vitro findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (novelty vs prior work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Some aspects of the work were already done by the team. Response: Revised the scope so that the work proposed is entirely new, both to us and to the state-of-the-art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate novelty relative to prior work (including your own) by revising aims and highlighting what is new in approach, measurements, or targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator (qualifications and leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: PI Vernita Gordon is very junior and does not have enough related publications. Response: PI published eight original research articles in leading microbiology and interdisciplinary journals (2015-2016). Leadership demonstrated via multidisciplinary teams and professional service; collaborators add deep expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence of productivity and leadership (recent publications, roles leading teams, biosketch) and emphasize complementary expertise of collaborators to address reviewers' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (connection to therapeutics and novelty of techniques)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: No explanation of how this study will lead to new targeted drug or treatment development. Response: Included new Preliminary Studies indicating molecular mechanisms underlying mechanical contributions of matrix components; points toward therapies using competitive binding or enzymatic degradation. Changed antibiotic-resistance work to focus on tobramycin, PEG-ylated tobramycin, and bicarbonate. Highlighted novel nature of rheology studies and that how viscoelastic mechanics impacts susceptibility to phagocytosis is unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain mechanistic links between findings and potential therapeutic strategies; specify targets and how results will guide therapy development; emphasize genuinely novel measurements or approaches versus standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (model choice and site consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Using three different mouse models, at two different geographical sites, could cause site-specific factors to affect outcome. Response: Now use only one mouse model at only one site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit unnecessary complexity in models and sites; prefer consistent, well-justified models and minimize confounding site-specific variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (statistical treatment and quantifiable hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Statistical treatment and identification of potential relationships were not discussed; lack of quantifiable hypotheses. Response: Expanded discussion of statistical treatment (Research Strategy & Vertebrate Animals). Indicate expected functional form of relationships where supported by physical understanding; elsewhere describe properties of the expected function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, quantifiable hypotheses and a detailed statistical plan (including expected functional forms or properties), and describe how relationships will be identified and tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (preliminary data and feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Not enough preliminary data to ensure success. Response: All preliminary studies are now published in peer-reviewed journals and have been referenced in the resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include strong, published preliminary data that directly support feasibility of key methods and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (clarity of experimental plans and methods detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Experimental plans unclear. Response: Clarified and increased detail in all Aims; expanded rheology plan and clarified which techniques are essential versus secondary (e.g., microrheology secondary to AFM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, stepwise methodological descriptions, state which techniques are primary versus contingency/secondary, and explain why chosen methods will answer the specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (sample size and animal numbers justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism: Requested number of mice not well-supported. Response: Expanded Vertebrate Animals; power calculations and animal usage table referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit power calculations and an animal usage table to justify numbers, and place these in the Vertebrate Animals section as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (sites, collaborators, and biosafety facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response: Now only sites and colleagues in Texas are involved. Criticism: Three performance sites, one foreign, would make collaboration difficult. Response: Removed the foreign participant. All animal work will be done in a certified animal facility and all in vitro work in BSL-2 laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional support, on-site facilities, biosafety compliance, and simplify collaborative arrangements when review concerns are raised about management or logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards / Biological safety level appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: P. aeruginosa is a BSL-2 organism; all animal work will be done in a certified animal facility and all in vitro work in BSL-2 laboratories. Response notes that the previous statement 'Any biological safety facility would be used' was incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the appropriate BSL level for the organism and that certified facilities meeting that level will be used; correct any ambiguous statements about biosafety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims (clear objectives and hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal's objective is to determine the impact of spatial structure and mechanics of P. aeruginosa biofilm infections in chronic wounds on virulence, antibiotic resistance, and immune evasion. Central hypothesis: spatial structure and mechanics are the major physical factors controlling pathogenicity, antibiotic resistance, and immune evasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a concise Specific Aims page with a clear central hypothesis, explicit objectives, and distinct, testable aims each with a working hypothesis and planned measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of spatial structure (imaging metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sophisticated imaging to determine, in three dimensions, the size, number, locations, and heterogeneous matrix content of bacterial aggregates in a mouse model of chronic wound infection; simultaneously measure density and distribution of neutrophils around aggregates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify imaging modalities (e.g., CLSM), quantitative image analysis approaches, and explicit structural metrics (aggregate size distribution, number density, 3D positions, neutrophil correlations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of mechanics (AFM and microrheology plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop technique using AFM microindentation and abradement of ex vivo biofilms; microrheology is secondary. AFM will be used in liquid; tapping mode for topography and stiffness maps; Force-Volume mapping and contact models (Hertz or Sneddon) to obtain elasticity; constant force mode for relaxation spectrum; Amplitude and Frequency Modulation to estimate G' and G''; microrheology in vivo attempted as secondary approach (two-particle passive or active magnetic beads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe primary mechanical measurement method in detail (instrument, modes, models), explain constraints (ex vivo vs in vivo) and rank methods by priority and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of structure and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Here 'spatial structure' means the size and number density of bacterial aggregates and the matrix heterogeneity within aggregates, and 'mechanics' means viscoelastic responses to applied forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear operational definitions for key concepts so reviewers can assess whether proposed measurements appropriately capture them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of model selection / literature grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale that P. aeruginosa is an important biofilm-forming human pathogen; discussion of differences between in vitro and in vivo biofilms; use CF lung infections as a test case to guide wound biofilms because of similar pressures and because wounds facilitate imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground choices in current literature, explain similarities/differences among model systems, and justify why chosen models are appropriate for the questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPS/matrix-component hypotheses and mechanistic links
rubrics_metrics.description: Most important EPS materials: Psl, Pel, alginate, and eDNA. Alginate chelates reactive oxygen species and prevents complement activation; Psl protects against antibiotics and blocks opsonin binding; Pel binds to eDNA and contributes to mechanics. Preliminary data link EPS composition changes to changes in mechanical metrics (G', G'', σY, EnergyY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate specific mechanistic hypotheses linking matrix components to mechanical properties and disease-relevant phenotypes, and propose experiments to test those links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data metrics and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary rheology data: plateau G' ~10x greater than plateau G''; material failure begins at yield strain εY and yield stress σY; EnergyY is energy cost to cause yielding. Example findings: increased alginate reduces EnergyY ~2/3 and plateau G' by 90%; increased Psl can rescue mechanical losses; AFM measurements show interbacterial cohesion changes (Psl increases work to separate cells 4-6×, Pel decreases it 20×).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present quantitative preliminary metrics (G', G'', σY, EnergyY) and explain how they inform the proposed experiments and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image analysis and quantitative metrics (expected dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quantitative image analysis in Matlab to turn micrographs into quantitative measurements; determine size distribution of aggregates, 3D positions and number density, and spatial distribution of neutrophils; expect aggregate size distribution to peak and then plateau as aggregates hit oxygen-limited size limits and width decrease over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the quantitative metrics to be extracted, expected temporal trajectories, and how to analyze correlations between structural metrics and biological outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport property measurement using tracers
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop technique by co-inoculating fluorescent beads and quantum dots of different sizes and surface functionalities into animal models with bacteria, and measure how spatial distribution of tracer particles changes with time to estimate effective diffusion constants and transport (including flow/animal movement). If transport properties change with time, add differently-labeled tracers at different timepoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use size- and surface-specific tracers to quantify effective diffusion/transport in vivo, and include plans to vary labeling/timepoints to capture temporal changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staining specificity and validation for matrix components
rubrics_metrics.description: Most stains for biofilm matrix materials also stain host tissue. Plan: use quantitative image analysis to distinguish differential binding (expect higher brightness in biofilm than tissue); validate by comparing biofilms that over-express specific EPS materials with WT biofilms. Specific stains: antibody and lectin for Psl, lectin for Pel, propidium iodide for eDNA, cationic dyes for alginate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate cross-reactivity, quantify signal-to-background, and validate stains using genetic over-expression/knockout controls and known stain sources/contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex vivo sample handling constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex vivo biopsy samples will be placed onto an agar plate and kept submerged within a growth broth and characterized using AFM in liquid; all tests will occur as quickly as possible after excision, always less than 12 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sample preservation/handling protocols and maximum delays to measurement to ensure sample properties remain representative of in vivo state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microrheology feasibility and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: In vivo microrheology (two-particle passive) can relate correlated particle motion to viscoelastic moduli using Stokes-Einstein relations; active microrheology with magnetic tweezers can apply stresses up to ~25 kPa. Microrheology in vivo has potential difficulties and is a secondary analysis technique intended to supplement primary AFM analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame microrheology as an ambitious but secondary approach, describe potential pitfalls, and explain how results would supplement primary ex vivo AFM data.
